content.title: About
content.content: A marble cake or cupcake is a tender sponge in which two batters – a light vanilla one and a dark chocolate one – are swirled together to create the characteristic marble pattern. It has a soft, slightly moist crumb and a balanced sweetness with hints of vanilla and cocoa.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The marble batter technique originated in Europe in the 19th century and quickly became a bakery staple.
The marble effect is achieved by folding small portions of dark batter into the light batter, leaving distinct streaks.
In many countries the marble cupcake is a traditional treat for holidays and family celebrations.
Numerous variations exist, adding nuts, dried fruit, or flavorings such as coffee or orange zest.
Marble cake is often used as a base for layered desserts, topped with frosting or glaze.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Provides carbohydrates that quickly supply the body with energy, making it a handy snack before activity.

items.title: Protein content
items.content: Eggs and dairy in the recipe contribute a modest amount of protein for tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The batter contains B1, B2 and B6 vitamins, important for metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Calcium and iron are present thanks to the milk and eggs.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Cocoa in the dark batter is rich in flavonoids, which may support heart health.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: The sweetness can raise blood glucose levels, especially for people with diabetes.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: The recipe contains eggs, milk and gluten, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Cake or cupcakes are calorie‑dense; moderate portions are advised for weight management.

items.title: Trans‑fat presence
items.content: Using margarine instead of butter may introduce trans fats, which are undesirable for cardiovascular health.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the cake as a standalone dessert, slice into portions and pair with fruit sauce, berry jam, or buttercream. Cupcakes are convenient to eat by hand and are often enjoyed for breakfast or as a snack alongside tea or coffee.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer storage (up to 1 week) refrigerate. Allow the cake to come to room temperature before serving for optimal texture.

content.title: About
content.content: Cottage cheese with vegetables is a soft curd cheese mixed with selected fresh vegetables (such as carrot, cucumber, tomato and herbs). The product has a mild creamy taste, a slight tang and a crunchy texture from the vegetables. It can be enjoyed as a snack, a filling for sandwiches, salads or baked dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cottage cheese is one of the oldest dairy products, known since ancient Egypt.
Combining cottage cheese with vegetables increases the bioavailability of vitamins, especially vitamin C from the veggies.
In many countries cottage cheese is a staple of low‑calorie diets because of its high protein and low fat content.
Vegetables are usually diced finely, making them easy to digest.
Cottage cheese products are available in low‑fat and full‑fat versions to suit different dietary needs.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Cottage cheese provides high‑quality dairy protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Calcium supports bone and tooth health.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals from vegetables
items.content: The added vegetables contribute vitamin C, vitamin A, potassium and dietary fiber, which aid immunity and digestion.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: A low‑fat version is suitable for weight‑management diets due to its modest calorie count.

items.title: Supports gut microbiota
items.content: Cottage cheese contains probiotic cultures that can help maintain a healthy intestinal flora.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance may experience bloating, gas or diarrhea after consuming cottage cheese.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Allergy to casein can cause skin rashes, swelling and, in severe cases, anaphylaxis.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some packaged versions contain added salt; individuals with hypertension should choose low‑sodium options.

items.title: Shelf life
items.content: Improper storage can lead to bacterial growth, so the product should be kept refrigerated.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy cottage cheese with vegetables straight from the pack, spread it on bread, use it as a filling for wraps, roll it in lettuce leaves, or mix it with boiled potatoes. Fresh herbs, a squeeze of lemon juice or a drizzle of olive oil can enhance the flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the product in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C in its original packaging or an airtight container. Once opened, it is best consumed within 5‑7 days. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.

pizza-cheese-and-vegetables-whole-wheat-.title: Cheese and Vegetable Pizza, Whole Wheat Thin Crust

content.title: About
content.content: A thin whole‑wheat crust pizza topped with cheese and vegetables is a balanced dish that provides whole grains, dairy protein, and a variety of vegetables. The crust is made from whole‑wheat flour, increasing fiber content, while the toppings include tomato sauce, mozzarella, bell pepper, mushrooms and onion.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole‑wheat crust retains more B‑vitamins and minerals than traditional white crust.
Tomatoes in the sauce are rich in lycopene, an antioxidant that becomes more bioavailable after cooking.
Traditional mozzarella is made from buffalo milk, but most commercial pizza uses cow’s milk.
Vegetables such as bell pepper and mushrooms add not only flavor but also vitamins A, C and D.
Thin crust bakes quickly, preserving a crisp texture and reducing overall calorie count.

items.title: High in Fiber
items.content: Whole‑wheat flour provides dietary fiber that supports digestive health and helps maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of Protein
items.content: Mozzarella and vegetables contribute both dairy and plant protein needed for tissue repair.

items.title: Vitamins and Minerals
items.content: Tomatoes, bell pepper and mushrooms supply vitamin C, vitamin A, potassium and iron, supporting immunity and cellular function.

items.title: Low in Saturated Fat
items.content: The thin crust and moderate cheese amount make this pizza lower in saturated fat compared with typical deep‑dish versions.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Lycopene from tomatoes and polyphenols from vegetables help combat free radicals.

items.title: Dairy Allergy
items.content: Mozzarella may trigger allergic reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or dairy protein allergy.

items.title: Sodium Content
items.content: Tomato sauce and cheese can contain notable amounts of salt; people monitoring sodium intake should watch portion size.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Whole‑wheat crust contains gluten and is unsuitable for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Caloric Density
items.content: Despite the thin crust, the combination of cheese and oil in the sauce makes the dish energy‑dense; portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Reheat the pizza in a oven at 200 °C for 5–7 minutes to retain a crisp crust. Slice into serving pieces and serve with a green salad or a light yogurt‑based dip.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftover pizza in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in a freezer‑safe bag for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before eating.

content.title: About
content.content: Roll is a ready‑to‑eat product made from whole wheat grains enriched with NS bran. It has a light crunchy texture, a mild nutty flavor, and is suitable for breakfast or as a snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: NS bran (non‑starch by‑product) contains more than 70 % dietary fiber.
Roll is produced without artificial colors or flavorings.
The product has a low glycemic index, making it suitable for blood‑sugar management.
NS bran is rich in B‑vitamins and minerals such as iron and magnesium.
Roll is packaged in single‑serve portions for easy storage and transport.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: NS bran provides a high amount of soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting normal digestion.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Fiber helps lower LDL‑cholesterol levels in the blood.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B2, B3 and folate contribute to energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Mineral complex
items.content: Iron, magnesium and zinc in the bran are important for blood formation and muscle function.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: Roll contains fewer calories than traditional bakery products, useful for weight control.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: The product may trigger allergic reactions in individuals sensitive to gluten.

items.title: High fiber content
items.content: Large portions can cause gastrointestinal discomfort in people unaccustomed to high fiber intake.

items.title: Phytic acid presence
items.content: Bran contains phytates, which may reduce the absorption of certain minerals when consumed in excess.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Roll can be eaten as a standalone snack, added to yogurt, kefir, salads, or used as a base for quick sandwiches. If desired, briefly warm the roll in a microwave to enhance its aroma.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store roll in a dry, cool place, tightly sealed. For long‑term storage, keep the product in the refrigerator to maintain crispness and prevent mold growth.

content.title: About
content.content: A vegetable sandwich on wheat bread is a light dish made with whole‑grain wheat bread, fresh vegetables (tomato, cucumber, lettuce, bell pepper, carrot) and often a light sauce or hummus. It is suitable for a quick snack, lunch or picnic and provides a variety of vitamins and fiber.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Wheat bread supplies slow‑release carbohydrates, helping to maintain steady energy levels.
Combining different vegetables increases antioxidant bioavailability through synergistic effects.
Vegetarian sandwiches often use hummus or avocado instead of mayonnaise, reducing saturated fat content.
Whole‑grain bread sandwiches support digestive health thanks to their fiber content.
No cooking is required, which preserves most of the vitamins in fresh vegetables.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain bread and vegetables provide dietary fiber that promotes regular bowel movements and a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Source of vitamins A and C
items.content: Tomatoes, carrots and bell peppers are high in beta‑carotene and vitamin C, which boost immunity and protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Absence of meat and use of light spreads make the sandwich suitable for heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: Hydration support
items.content: Fresh vegetables have a high water content, helping to maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Phytonutrients in vegetables (e.g., lycopene and lutein) protect vision and may lower the risk of chronic diseases.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: People with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity should choose a gluten‑free bread alternative.

items.title: Possible bacterial contamination
items.content: Sliced vegetables can harbor Salmonella or E. coli, so they should be washed thoroughly.

items.title: High sodium in sauces
items.content: Store‑bought sauces may contain a lot of salt; homemade low‑sodium options are preferable.

items.title: Food interactions
items.content: Acids from tomatoes enhance iron absorption from plant sources, which is beneficial but may need monitoring in certain medical conditions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Spread hummus, avocado mash, or a light yogurt sauce on the bread, then layer lettuce, tomato slices, cucumber, carrot ribbons and bell pepper strips. Cut the sandwich in half and serve immediately or wrap it for a work‑day snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: A prepared sandwich can be kept in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours, wrapped in parchment or placed in an airtight container. Store bread in a dry place and keep vegetables separate to prevent sogginess.
